findings.title: Public group members page silently truncated to 50 members
findings.body: The members endpoint now defaults to a page size of 50 for every group (previously non-automatic groups returned all members and automatic groups were capped at 200). The public members page (`group/members.hbs`) renders `members` with `{{#each}}` and has no pagination controls, and the shared `Discourse.Group` model also defaults `limit: 50`. For any non-automatic group with more than 50 members, users see only the first 50 and have no way to reach the rest. This is a functional regression on the public group page.

findings.title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
findings.body: `totalPages` uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which should be `Math.ceil`. With 50 members and limit 50 it reports 2 pages (header shows "1/2") when only one exists. `next` then sets offset to min(offset+limit, user_count) = 50, which requests an empty page, so the admin sees an empty member list. With 100 members it reports 3 pages.

findings.title: Remove link is rendered for automatic groups because `automatic` is looked up on the member
findings.body: Inside `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}` the item context is the member User object, not the group, so `{{#unless automatic}}` resolves `automatic` against the user and is always falsy. The remove link therefore appears for automatic groups too. The server rejects those removals with a 422, and `removeMember` in the admin controller and model has no failure handler, so the click appears to do nothing. The flag needs to come from the controller or be passed into the item view.

findings.title: create ignores alias_level even though the client now sends it
findings.body: `Discourse.Group#asJSON` now includes `alias_level`, and the new-group form shows the alias-level selector. `create` assigns only name and visible, so the chosen alias_level is silently dropped and the group gets the default. The PR rewrote `create` but left this gap in place.

findings.title: Removing a non-member raises RecordNotFound instead of succeeding
findings.body: `group.users.delete(user_id)` with an integer id makes Rails 4 look the record up with `find` on the association, which raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound when that user is not a member. The old PATCH path tolerated removing non-members, and the deleted spec ('succeeds silently when removing non-members') asserted that. A double-click or a stale member list now produces a 404 that the Ember client does not handle.

findings.title: limit/offset are unvalidated: negative values cause a 500, and limit has no cap
findings.body: `limit` and `offset` come straight from `params.to_i`. A negative `limit` produces `LIMIT -1`, which PostgreSQL rejects, so the request fails with a 500; a negative offset fails the same way. There is also no upper bound on limit, so a single request can pull the full membership of any visible group. Clamp limit to a sane range and floor offset at 0.

findings.title: GET /groups/:name/members.json response shape changed from an array to an object
findings.body: The endpoint now returns `{members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}}` instead of a bare array of users, and the default page size changed. Any other consumer of this public JSON endpoint (plugins, API clients) will break silently. The PR description does not mention the contract change.

findings.title: Admin update silently resets visible for clients using the old nested params
findings.body: `update` now reads flat top-level params and no longer reads `group[...]`, and the PATCH membership path is removed. A client still sending the old nested payload (`group[name]`, `group[visible]`) gets `params[:visible]` nil, so `group.visible` is set to false without any error. The name change is also silently skipped.

findings.title: remove_member spec uses PUT although the route is DELETE
findings.body: The route added in config/routes.rb is `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`, but this spec sends `xhr :put, :remove_member`. Controller specs do not enforce the HTTP verb, so the test passes while production would never reach the action with PUT. The verb mismatch goes untested. The other remove test (line 125) correctly uses :delete.

findings.title: No positive test for updating a non-automatic group
findings.body: The `.update` context only checks that renaming an automatic group is ignored. The rename, visible, and alias_level paths for normal groups, which are the main behavior of the rewritten `update` action, have no test. The old test covering name changes for regular groups was removed.

findings.title: New public members endpoint and its pagination have no spec
findings.body: The `members` action changed its response shape, default limit, and query logic, and the group members UI now depends on the meta fields. No spec in this PR exercises pagination, meta values, the 50-member default, or access to hidden groups through `find_group`.

findings.title: Stale selector targets the user-selector id that this PR renamed
findings.body: `input#group-users` still sets a 600px width, but group.hbs now passes `id="user-selector"`, so this rule no longer matches anything. The layout rule is dead and the input falls back to the generic width.
